notes: Scope: I verified the four R2 findings plus the actual complete indexes. Files read: R2 review.json; review2-resolution-notes.json; he-kesod.xml and en-kesod.xml in full; the complete Heidenheim index (850 lines); the Marmorstein index lines 360–709 (Shacharit repetition tail through end of Musaf); the expanded index lines 1–799 and 2500–3322 (front, early services, Torah/Shofar through end of Musaf); new-registry-records.json lines 1–400 and 700–1441; both-sequences.json documentary_sequence and the expanded Veyeetayu section; feature-check-structured.json; full-service-report.json; resolved-scope-checks.json; final-build-schema-report.json; registry-check.log; naming-final.log; xml-manifest.json.

I did not read every line of the expanded Shacharit block (lines 800–2499). For its Attah Hu and Berikh Shemeh tests I relied on feature-check-structured.json, which shows frankfurt_am_main as the only Frankfurt rite feature, and on the R2 closure.

Residual design note, not a finding: the חזן note before kesod_siach stays inside the canonical root div. A transclusion of the whole prayer (naaritzekha_venaqdishkha_kesod@heidenheim) therefore brings this edition's two source roles along, once each. This is the 'at minimum' option R2 allowed, and the expanded spine is consistent with it because it adds no Kesod rubric. If a future edition needs Kesod without these cues, split it into a speaker-free word home plus a documentary wrapper.

The schema build covers 756 files: 731 identical to previously validated XML and 25 freshly validated. The registry has 0 errors and 0 warnings; its only note is an unrelated unregistered-contributor INFO for tanakh-jps-1917-en/isaiah.xml.

Approving data_encoding and generated_encoding covers the encoded data and the generated index XML. It is not final export approval. Corrected-state renders and the full 36-state compile are a separate QA step (see remaining_export_checks).
